card.name: special-population evidence check
card.exclude_reason: A conditional question stem alone does not establish that a special-population or trial-derived regimen applies; unknown demographic or comorbidity facts do not imply the special-population rule is satisfied, and absence of a retrieved special-population span must not eliminate otherwise indicated treatments.
card.procedure: 1) List the patient's stated qualifying demographic, comorbidity, and severity conditions. 2) Retrieve both product-label indication spans and any special-population or trial-derived regimen evidence. 3) Check whether the special-population evidence's qualifying conditions are actually present in this patient. 4) If present, weigh that regimen against general label indications; if absent, rely on general indications. 5) Select the option supported by the applicable evidence tier, not by label-span presence alone.
card.counterexample_explanation: In the Mycoplasma case the correct answer follows directly from standard organism-specific diagnostic and treatment evidence, with no special-population qualifier present; forcing a special-population retrieval step would risk displacing the correct standard answer. In the eclampsia case the correct management follows the standard condition-specific regimen for the stated pregnancy context, and no additional demographic or trial-derived qualifier is required; the added step must therefore be inert when the qualifying condition is absent, preserving these successes.

card.name: check_span_before_context_modifier
card.exclude_reason: Applies only when the question asks about an interaction/co-medication concern; a plain dose or route question without an interaction framing is out of region, and unknown interaction facts never imply safety.
card.procedure: 1) Identify the interaction/co-medication concern the question is testing. 2) Retrieve source spans for each candidate option's interaction profile. 3) If a span explicitly states the interaction or its absence, use it. 4) If no span addresses the interaction, do not infer safety from missing text; fall back to the best-established general property of the option. 5) Prefer the option whose interaction status is directly supported over one supported only by an unstated assumption.

card.name: tie_break_only_on_decisive_span
card.exclude_reason: Applies only when the question frames an interaction/co-medication concern; a plain dose or route question without interaction framing is out of region, and unknown interaction facts never imply safety.
card.procedure: 1) Identify the interaction/co-medication concern being tested. 2) Retrieve spans for each candidate option's interaction profile. 3) If a span explicitly states the interaction or its absence, use it. 4) If two options both have matching spans, do not break the tie with a monitoring precaution or warning; require a decisive span (contraindication, restriction, or explicit preference). 5) If no decisive span exists, mark the choice ambiguous rather than preferring one option. 6) Absence of a retrieved span never eliminates a treatment.

The procedure preserves them because it still selects the option with explicit span support and only changes behavior when two options are equally supported and no decisive differentiator span exists.

card.name: interaction_span_before_absence_inference

card.procedure: 1) Name the co-medication or interaction the question tests. 2) Retrieve spans for each candidate option's interaction/absorption profile. 3) Select the option whose interaction status is directly stated by a span. 4) If no span addresses the interaction, do not treat missing text as safety or as exclusion; fall back to the option's best-established general property. 5) Do not let a monitoring precaution or warning outrank a directly supported interaction fact.
